messages.author: befc31f30774e5bc
messages.subject: Plotting maps!
parts:
These are related to creating figures.

1) I cannot seem to get the border of CA plotted on top of my raster image. I've tried many different packages, and follow directions well, but alas, I'm stuck.

2) I have the same issue with changing the color scheme of the raster rainbow. I'd like to illustrate the spread of occurrence points throughout CA, and use the alt data from worldclim, but I don't want the same color scheme as for the climate data. I think it's confusing to a reader. Preferably, black and white.

Any simple suggestions?

Thanks, Iara

--
Iara Lacher
MESM - Bren School for Environmental Science and Management
PhD Candidate- UC Davis Ecology Graduate Group

messages.author: 80d591788d62f6ed
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Plotting maps!
parts:
Lara,

1) It is probably a projection issue.  What are the projections of the vector (California boundary) and raster layers you are working with?  Have you defined the projection of your raster in your script?  To define the projection of your raster, use projection() from the {raster} package.  If the projections are different I recommend you transform the vector layer to the same as the raster using spTransform() from the {sp} package.

If you provide the projection information, I may be able to give you some more specific suggestions.

Good luck,
Eric

You may have already tried these combinations, but NCEAS has example code for different options of overlaying vectors on rasters:

http://www.nceas.ucsb.edu/scicomp/usecases/CreateMapsWithRGraphics

I‘m sure someone can figure it out if you show us the code you’re currently using. You could drop the relevant raster / shapefile in Dropbox (UsesaveRDS()to save your post-processed raster object) and provide the link.
